problems: Orange and green shirt sleeves, blue trouser legs and blocky closed footwear remain conspicuous. Linen aprons over these defaults do not establish an unmistakable Bronze Age.
The four everyday kits share almost the same body silhouette. Their distinction relies heavily on handheld objects and small front details that will weaken at stream scale.
The water carrier's chest wrap reads as a disconnected rectangular patch. The weaver's shoulder wrap reads as a chest stripe, while the elder's shawl resembles two stiff vest panels.
The field tender's sun cloth presents as a tall rectangular slab rather than cloth resting on the crown and draping behind the neck.
The trader repeats the elder's pale cap and paired front panels. Its lapis strip and delicate scales are insufficient to establish a visibly foreign caravan leader.
Solid hip-mounted skirt boxes and the priest's long rigid robe need gait testing: they enclose both leg paths and risk visible leg penetration during movement.

ALL KITS: no kit hides 'sleeves', 'trousers' or 'shoes', so every figure still wears the base long-sleeved shirt, full-length trousers (blue jeans on the orange model) and black modern shoes. A skirt or tunic is just layered over today's clothes, which breaks the brief's 'never today's clothes recoloured' rule and the bible's linen-skirt/sandals rule.
ALL KITS: the 'sandals' on Field Tender and the Leader are pants:dark boxes (0.205x0.115x0.285) that enclose the base shoe. They render as chunky blue boots or sneakers, not sandals.

PAIRS COLLIDE: Water Carrier (jar in left hand) and Reed Weaver (basket in left hand) have the same silhouette. Field Tender (long hoe, right hand) and Village Elder (long staff, right hand) also match, and both wear the same knee tunic with a belt. At stream scale there are two silhouettes, not four.

Water Carrier: the 'shoulder cloth' (hips part at [0.1,0.43,0.17], accent:dark, rot z -0.18) renders as a tilted slab floating off the chest. It reads as a phone or tablet, not a cloth over the shoulder. The tied-hair bun is a tiny dome that hardly shows. The wrap-skirt overlap panel is offset and looks misaligned.

Field Tender: the headcloth is a stacked cream box sitting on the hair box, so it reads as a tall cube hat (fez or chef hat), not a draped sun cloth. The hoe has a small blade at the top of a vertical shaft and reads as a flag or hatchet.

Reed Weaver: the torso box uses 'shirt', the base colour, so the top is unchanged. The 'broad shoulder wrap' is a dark horizontal stripe across the chest (accent:dark at y 0.49), which reads as a striped T-shirt. The pants:light under-kilt shows as grey shorts, and the apron over jeans is a modern shop apron. Its cape sits behind the figure and cannot be seen.

Village Elder: the two shawl lapels are thick, separate slabs that don't drape over the shoulders and look like two books stuck to the chest. The sphere cap is a flat cream oval on top of dark hair and reads as a bald spot or skullcap. The tunic is knee-length like Field Tender's, so the elder isn't visibly older or grander.

High Priest (strongest kit): the base hair shows as a black band across the forehead between headdress and face, which reads as sunglasses. A pale tab drops onto the face centre. The chest sun disc (#b68942, 0.275 wide) sits on top of a sash coloured by 'hat', which is gold on this wearer, so the symbol of office blends into the sash. The thin vertical stub above the disc makes it look like a gear on a pin. Base black shoes show under the robe.

Caravan Leader: nothing says 'from far away'. It reuses the Village Elder's two-lapel shawl and the Priest's stacked-cylinder-and-dome headcloth. The headcloth is in shirt:light, a pink dome on this wearer, and reads as a bald head. It has the same black 'sunglasses' hair band. The striped mantle stripes are all on the back cape, which can't be seen from the front. The 'lapis bead collar' is one flat blue bar floating at z 0.23, like a name badge. The grey accent diamond floats on the belly. The balance is too small to read at stream scale. The jeans and boot-sandals remain.
fix:
Water Carrier: Remove the exposed modern shirt and trouser treatment; use a short linen wrap, bare lower legs and strapped sandals. Connect the diagonal chest cloth continuously over one shoulder to its back section, fitted close to the torso. Keep the excellent clay jar and make the tied bun visible above the hair silhouette. Field Tender: Use a distinct sleeveless, knee-length belted tunic with bare arms and shins. Flatten the crown cloth and extend a fitted rear neck drape, eliminating the tall slab silhouette. Thicken the hoe shaft and enlarge its bronze blade slightly. Reed Weaver: Replace the modern shirt-and-apron read with a short woven wrap and a broad, connected one-shoulder mantle. Keep its hem distinctly shorter than the tender's. Give the basket a chunky raised rim and broad woven bands rather than tiny surface details. Village Elder: Join the front shawl panels across the shoulders into one continuous wool garment; broaden the upper-back silhouette and add a substantial contrasting hem. Replace visible trousers with an appropriate long wrap and sandals; retain the walking stick. High Priest: Preserve the tall sun staff, tiered headwrap and oversized bronze medallion. Fit the diagonal sash flush around the torso and shoulder instead of reading as a rigid board. Segment and skin the robe for walking, keeping its long ceremonial silhouette without trapping both legs inside a rigid shell. River Trader: Establish a separate foreign silhouette with a broad asymmetric fringed mantle, bold stripes continuing over the shoulders, and a banded headwrap unlike the priest's or elder's. Enlarge the lapis collar into a readable upper-chest shape and thicken the balance beam, supports and pans. Replace modern sleeves, trousers and footwear. Across all kits, use hollow fitted garment shells, attach cloth convincingly at shoulders and waist, and validate both avatar variants in motion at the actual 40-degree stream view. / GLOBAL: Every everyday kit, the leader and the priest need hide ['hat','accessory','trousers','shoes'], plus 'sleeves' wherever arms are bare. Replace the sandal 'boxes' with real sandals on each leg: a sole box [0,-0.785,0.04] size [0.2,0.03,0.28] in #8a663d and an ankle strap box [0,-0.73,0.02] size [0.19,0.03,0.21] in #6d4c32. Where a kit has sleeves, add short cap sleeves on armL/armR at [0,-0.08,0] size [0.17,0.18,0.19] in the tunic colour. Any kit with headgear should also hide 'hair' or bring the headgear down to y≈0.22 at the front so no hair band shows across the forehead. Give each kit one unique silhouette carrier and no shared props.
WATER CARRIER: Move the pottery jar onto the head (head bone, sphere [0,0.45,0] size [0.28,0.3,0.28] in #b17a49, neck cylinder [0,0.62,0] size [0.13,0.08,0.13], ring pad [0,0.34,0] size [0.24,0.04,0.24] in #d2bb87) and steady it with one raised arm, or leave the hands empty. That is a unique, top-readable silhouette. Lengthen the wrap skirt to mid-calf (centre y -0.3, height 0.62) with the overlap panel flush (x 0.08, z 0.16, no rotation). Bare arms and bare legs. Replace the chest slab with a real shoulder cloth: one box over the left shoulder [0.17,0.56,0] size [0.2,0.07,0.34], a front drop [0.17,0.42,0.155] size [0.18,0.26,0.03] and a back drop, all accent:dark and touching the body. Make the bun a clear knot at [0,0.36,-0.1] size 0.16.
FIELD TENDER: Knee tunic with cap sleeves, bare lower arms and legs, sandals. Hide hair and rebuild the sun headcloth as a low cap [0,0.3,0] size [0.36,0.08,0.34] with side lappets hanging to the shoulders at [±0.17,0.1,-0.03] size [0.04,0.32,0.28] and a back flap to the neck. The draped outline is what reads as a sun cloth. Carry the hoe over the right shoulder, tilted about 0.6 rad, with a broad bronze blade (#b68942, about 0.26x0.05x0.14) set at right angles to the shaft so it reads as an adze-hoe, not a flag.
REED WEAVER: Drop the 'shirt' torso and the chest stripe. Wear a one-shoulder wrap: a diagonal box across the chest from the left shoulder to the right hip (hips [0.02,0.3,0.155] size [0.2,0.72,0.03], rot z 0.55, accent:dark) with a matching back piece. Pair it with a knee kilt in pants:light (centre y -0.12, height 0.4, no grey 'shorts' showing below), bare arms, bare legs and bare feet. Replace the hand basket with a tall bundle of reeds on the back: 5–6 cylinders on the cape bone in #d2bb87/#b68942, rising 0.35 above the head, tied with a #6d4c32 band. That gives a spiky, unique outline from above.
VILLAGE ELDER: Ankle-length robe (lower box to y -0.7) so the elder stands apart from the knee tunics. Hide trousers and shoes and add sandals. Make the shawl actually drape: add shoulder boxes [±0.17,0.57,0] size [0.2,0.06,0.36] in hat:dark joining the back cape to two thin front panels (depth 0.03, z 0.17, flush with the robe), plus a visible accent fringe at their hems. Replace the skullcap sphere with a wrapped cap or a hood fold, or drop it. Give the staff a distinct crook or knob top (a curved hook from 2–3 boxes, or a #b68942 sphere) so it isn't confused with a tool.
HIGH PRIEST: Keep the long robe and the sun staff, which are good. Hide hair and the base shoes and add sandals. Lower the headdress so its bottom band covers the forehead at y≈0.23, add a turquoise (#429d9b) wrap band, and remove the pale tab over the face. Use fixed office colours for the mantle: an ochre #b68942 mantle over both shoulders with a #429d9b woven border, visible at the front. Don't take the mantle colour from the 'hat' role. Enlarge the chest sun disc to 0.36 diameter in bright #e2b34b with a #b68942 rim, set on the bare cream robe above the sash line (or route the sash under it). Replace the single vertical stub with two neck cords. Optionally make the headdress 0.08 taller so the priest is the tallest figure.
CARAVAN LEADER: Stop reusing the Elder's lapels and the Priest's dome. Give the leader a full-length striped mantle wrapped diagonally over one shoulder, with 3–4 horizontal accent/#ead7aa bands on the front as well as the back. Add a distinctive headcloth: a tall wrapped cylinder in #d2bb87 with a long tail hanging down the back to mid-back (cape bone), hair hidden. Build the lapis collar as a broad ring around the neck (hips [0,0.6,0.02], cylinder size [0.46,0.05,0.4], #365f86) with a row of #429d9b bead spheres along its front edge, sitting on the body rather than floating. Delete the floating grey diamond. Enlarge the balance (beam 0.46, pans 0.18 diameter in #b68942) and hold it out on the left. Add a travel pack or bale of folded textiles on the back (cape bone, about 0.4x0.35x0.2). Bare legs and leather sandals with ankle straps.
